'''Magdalena Tulli''' (born '''Maddalena Flavia Tulli'''; 20 October 1955 in [[Warsaw]], Poland) is a [[Polish literature|Polish novelist]] and translator.<ref>[http://www.kosciuszkofoundation.org/EV_May04_8.html ''The Kosciusko Foundation''] {{webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20040503153552/http://www.kosciuszkofoundation.org/EV_May04_8.html |date=2004-05-03 }}.</ref>

==Life and career==
Tulli has an Italian father and a Polish-Jewish mother, and grew up partially in Italy.<ref name=":0" /> She graduated from high school in 1974 in Warsaw and obtained a Master's degree in biology at the [[University of Warsaw]] in 1979. She then worked six months at the [[Henryk Arctowski Polish Antarctic Station]]. In 1983, she earned a PhD at the Institute of Biology and Zoology of the [[Polish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.ppibl.ibl.waw.pl/mediawiki/index.php?title=Magdalena_TULLI|title=Magdalena TULLI|last=Sęczek|first=Marlena|date=2018-04-22|website=Polscy pisarze i badacze literatury przełomu XX i XXI wieku|language=pl|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref>

Tulli made her literary debut in 1995 with the prose poem ''Sny i kamienie''.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://culture.pl/en/artist/magdalena-tulli |title=Magdalena Tulli |website=Culture.pl |access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref> She is a member of the [[Stowarzyszenie Pisarzy Polskich|Polish Writers' Association]]. Her works have been translated into many languages. In 2012, she won the [[Gdynia Literary Prize]] for her book ''Włoskie szpilki'' ("Italian High Heels").<ref name=":0" /> In the same year, her novel ''[[In Red]]'', translated by [[Bill Johnston (translator)|Bill Johnston]], was shortlisted for the [[Best Translated Book Award]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.rochester.edu/College/translation/threepercent/2012/04/10/2012-best-translated-book-award-finalists-fiction-and-poetry/|title=2012 Best Translated Book Award Finalists: Fiction and Poetry|date=2012-04-10|website=Three Percent|publisher=University of Rochester|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref> She received five nominations for the [[Nike Award]] - Poland's most prominent literary prize. Her style has been characterized as [[Postmodern literature|postmodern]] and [[metafiction]]al.<ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://culture.pl/en/artist/magdalena-tulli|title=Magdalena Tulli|last=Gliński|first=Mikołaj|date=2012|work=Culture.pl|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref>

She translated a number of books including [[Marcel Proust]]'s ''[[La Fugitive]]'', [[Italo Calvino]]'s ''The Watcher'' and [[Fleur Jaeggy]]'s ''La paura del cielo''.<ref name=":0" />

== Reception ==
''[[In Red]]'' has been reviewed by Kirsten Lodge for the ''[[Slavic and East European Journal]]''.<ref name=":4">{{cite journal  |last=Lodge |first=Kirsten |date=September 2012 |title=Review Article: Recent Polish Literature: Fantasy, Time, and Intertwining Worlds  |journal=[[Slavic and East European Journal]] |volume=56 |pages=447–450 |jstor=41698563 |id={{EBSCOhost|84426729}} |number=3}}</ref>

==Works==
*''Sny i kamienie'' 1995. (''Dreams and Stones'', [[Archipelago Books]] 2004).
*''W czerwieni'' 1998. (''In red'', Archipelago Books 2011).
*''Tryby'' 2003. (''Moving Parts'', Archipelago Books 2005).
*''Skaza'' 2006. (''Flaw'', Archipelago Books 2007)<ref name="wyz1">[http://wyborcza.pl/1,76842,4459294.html Magdalena Tulli], ''[[Gazeta Wyborcza]]'' (in Polish), September 4, 2007</ref>
*''Kontroler snów'' 2007, (Wydawnictwo ''Nisza'')
*''Włoskie szpilki'' 2011, (Wydawnictwo ''Nisza'')<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://culture.pl/pl/dzielo/magdalena-tulli-wloskie-szpilki |language=pl |title=Magdalena Tulli, "Włoskie szpilki" |access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref>
*''Szum'', 2014 (Wydawnictwo ''Znak'')<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://culture.pl/pl/dzielo/magdalena-tulli-szum |language=pl |title=Magdalena Tulli, "Szum" |access-date=16 November 2022}}</ref>
*''Ten i tamten las'', 2017 (Wydawnictwo ''Wilk i Król'')
*''Jaka piękna iluzja. W rozmowie z Justyną Dąbrowską'', 2017 (Wydawnictwo "Znak")
